title: Today's top defense-tech headlines
big: 46 new stories since the last brief. The busiest areas: drones & air autonomy and allies & theaters.

stories.h: Lockheed Martin Receives $694M Air Force Contract for Hypersonic Missile Production
stories.what: Lockheed Martin has a $694 million Department of War contract for the ARRW hypersonic missile, the Air Force said. The post Lockheed Martin Receives $694M Air Force Contract for Hypersonic Missile Production first appeared on Executive Gov .
stories.you: Weapons stockpiles are short, so anyone who can make missiles and rocket motors faster and cheaper has buyers.

stories.h: Northrop Grumman gets $56M to upgrade one MQ-4C Triton drone
stories.what: The U.S. Navy has ordered a $56 million retrofit for a single MQ-4C Triton, paying Northrop Grumman to install the B7 retrofit material kit on one of its high-altitude maritime surveillance drones.
stories.you: Drones are becoming the military's default purchase, so volume, price and reliability decide who wins.

stories.h: Army selects Lockheed Martin for billion-dollar Future Interceptor program
stories.what: Under a cost-sharing arrangement, Lockheed is expected to kick in $423 million for the project while Uncle Sam provides about $660 million. The post Army selects Lockheed Martin for billion-dollar Future Interceptor program appeared first on DefenseScoop .
stories.you: Missile defense is one of the biggest budget lines this decade, and its software and sensors are open to newcomers.

stories.h: From tanks to space, Norway and Germany forge ahead with ‘Hansa’ defense pact
stories.what: German tank maker KNDS and Norway’s Ritek have begun producing Leopard 2A8 tanks in Norway, adding a land-based industrial foothold to a security partnership spanning submarines, missiles and military operations in Europe’s north.
stories.you: More of the military's sensing and communications now runs through orbit, and new suppliers are getting in.

stories.h: PNNL-Led Consortium Applies AI to Battery Manufacturing Scale-Up
stories.what: PNNL took the helm of the DOE-backed BattMan Accelerator, uniting three other national labs and five universities on battery scale-up. The post PNNL-Led Consortium Applies AI to Battery Manufacturing Scale-Up first appeared on Executive Gov .
stories.you: Software that decides what to look at and what to hit is where the most value is moving.

watch.why: Around November 3. Whether US commercial growth keeps outpacing government revenue.

idea.why: Low-probability-of-intercept mesh radios that keep swarms coordinated under jamming. Autonomy at scale needs links that survive. Fiber works for one drone, not a swarm.
